title: Maximum Subarray
statement: Given a nonempty list `nums`, return the largest possible sum of any contiguous subarray. The subarray must contain at least one element.

predict_steps.prompt: After processing up through index 3 (value 4), what is the best sum ending at that index?
predict_steps.hint: Starting fresh at 4 beats carrying a negative prefix.

predict_steps.prompt: The famous subarray 4,-1,2,1 sums to what?

reference_solution:
def max_subarray(nums):
    best = nums[0]
    cur = nums[0]
    for i in range(1, len(nums)):
        x = nums[i]
        cur = max(x, cur + x)
        best = max(best, cur)
    return best

viva.question: What is the time cost of Kadane versus trying every subarray?
expected_points: each index updates a best sum ending here once
the global answer is tracked alongside the local best

viva.question: What breaks if you allow an empty subarray on an all-negative input?
expected_points: the statement requires a nonempty subarray
the answer is the largest single element when all values are negative
resetting to zero would invent an empty sum of zero
empty sums violate the at-least-one-element rule

viva.question: Why reset the running sum instead of extending it when the running sum goes bad?
expected_points: extending a negative prefix cannot help a future optimum
starting fresh at the current index restores a valid nonempty candidate
the global max still remembers earlier better segments
the invariant is best-ending-here versus best-anywhere
